name: Morning Again
label: Revelation
lede: A South Florida vegan straight edge band that ran through two singers, three drummers and a future New Found Glory guitarist in three years, made one album for Revelation, and broke up four months after it came out.

eras.title: A sister band to Culture
eras.text: John Wylie of Culture started Morning Again in Cooper City, Florida, and the two bands swapped members constantly. The first year produced a demo, a 12" about AOL and child abduction, a tour, two firings and a new singer from Ohio.

years.h: John Wylie starts Morning Again in Cooper City, Florida
years.p: Culture guitarist John Wylie forms Morning Again with singer [[Damien Moyal|b655a47c-28f5-466d-aba1-4d607e4f598a]], guitarist Michael Wolz, bassist Eric Ervin and drummer Louie Long. The band is straight edge, vegan, anti-religious and anti-government.

years.h: The Cleanest War: Morning Again's debut 12"
years.p: Five songs cut in January at Studio 13 in Deerfield Beach with Jeremy Staska, out on Conquer the World. America On Line warns about internet dependency and surveillance, in 1996.
years.xp:
Minus One was inspired by the abduction and murder of Adam Walsh; Remedy imagines authorities sitting on a cure, after the film Outbreak. According to Wikipedia, reviewers liked Moyal's delivery but found the internet song obscure at the time.

A demo tape had come out February 9. The vinyl lagged the CD by months.

years.h: Morning Again's first tour ends at Cheers, Coconut Grove
years.p: Morning Again's first North American tour runs May 27 to June 12, 1996, with a June 11 stop at Cheers in Coconut Grove, Florida.

years.h: Damien Moyal and Eric Ervin fired after the tour
years.p: According to Wikipedia, John Wylie's band fires singer Damien Moyal and bassist Eric Ervin over creative conflicts right after the 1996 tour. Moyal later fronts [[As Friends Rust|2f106f2f-5990-4f50-9590-3fa8da941f98]].

years.h: Chad Gilbert's stint on bass for Morning Again
years.p: Wikipedia lists [[Chad Gilbert|4ed8c877-0036-44c7-bf6f-4c9c8e8ccedb]], later of [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]], as Morning Again's bassist for part of 1996, one of several players to pass through that year.

years.h: Kevin Byers moves from Ohio to sing for Morning Again
years.p: John Wylie meets Kevin Byers at an Outcast show in Dayton, Ohio, and asks what he'll do next. Byers thinks he's being offered bass; it's the singer's job. He moves to Florida with almost nothing.

years.h: Two Morning Again 7"s: Intention, and a split with Shoulder
years.p: Morning Again put out a self-titled 7" on Intention Records and a split 7" with Shoulder on Moo Cow Records.

eras.title: Martyrs in a van
eras.text: With Kevin Byers out front, Morning Again became a touring machine in the US and Europe, next to Converge and Agnostic Front. Revelation signed them, the album came out, and the van broke before the band did.

years.h: Matthew Thomas replaces Louie Long on drums
years.p: Original Morning Again drummer Louie Long leaves; Matthew Thomas takes over.

years.h: Martyr 12" on Good Life
years.p: Morning Again's first record for Belgium's Good Life, the same year as My Statement of Life in a Dying World 7" on Immigrant Sun and the Hand of Hope collection.

years.h: Eleven months on the road with Converge and Agnostic Front
years.p: From November 1997 to October 1998 Morning Again tour the US and Europe with bands including [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]], playing Syracuse Hardcore Fest and shows in Germany and the Netherlands.

years.h: Kevin Byers sings the Revelation album with a sore throat
years.p: Morning Again record As Tradition Dies Slowly in twelve days at Studio 13. Byers was sick throughout, and says you can hear his voice burn out from the first song to the last.

years.h: Guitarist Joseph Simmons fired three weeks after the session
years.p: Joseph Simmons plays guitar on As Tradition Dies Slowly, then is fired three weeks later. Stephen Looker replaces him and gets the album credit without playing on it.

years.src: Wikipedia: As Tradition Dies Slowly · No Echo
years.h: As Tradition Dies Slowly · Revelation
years.p: Morning Again's only full-length of their original run: seven new songs and three re-recordings, art by [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]] of [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]]. It spends nine weeks on CMJ's Loud Rock chart, peaking at No. 22.
years.xp: Byers says Revelation just felt right compared with the other labels circling. Produced by Jeremy Staska, mastered by Alan Douches. It was the band's first release to chart at all, including No. 50 on FMQB's Metal Detector.

years.h: Morning Again break up and skip CMJ
years.p: Morning Again split in October 1998 and cancel their CMJ Music Marathon slot. Kevin Byers lists a van breakdown that killed a US tour, burnout, and his newborn daughter back home.
years.xp:
John Wylie was also pulled toward new projects, including his label Eulogy Recordings and the band Where Fear and Weapons Meet. The split came four months after As Tradition Dies Slowly was released.

Earlier that year the band also put out a split with [[25 ta Life|7be13e13-6362-4e97-aca7-edf7908cbeab]] on Good Life and the To Die a Bitter Death 7" on Immigrant Sun.

eras.title: Reunions under other names
eras.text: Morning Again kept coming back for one-offs, sometimes under the name of an old record. Eulogy, Wylie's label, kept the catalog in print.

years.h: Back as "Cleanest War" with Damien Moyal singing
years.p: Morning Again reunite with their fired original singer, Damien Moyal, and play under the name of their first record.

years.h: The Fallen... The Few That Remain on Eulogy
years.p: A Morning Again collection on John Wylie's own label, Eulogy Recordings.

years.h: An Orlando reunion billed as "Hand of Hope"
years.p: Morning Again play Orlando under the name of their 1997 collection, with Moyal and Ervin back. Hand of the Martyr gathers the early records on Alveran and Eulogy.

eras.title: Groezrock, Japan, and Revelation again
eras.text: Kevin Byers and Damien Moyal took turns out front as Morning Again became a festival band in Europe and Japan. Twenty years after the album, Revelation put out new songs.

years.h: Morning Again play Groezrock in Belgium
years.p: Kevin Byers fronts Morning Again at Belgium's Groezrock festival, the first big stage of the reunion years.

years.h: Two singers, one year: Ieperfest and Japan
years.p: Damien Moyal sings at Ieperfest in Belgium; Kevin Byers takes Morning Again to Japan for the Bloodaxe festival in Tokyo and a show in Nagoya.

years.h: Morning Again play This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia
years.p: Revelation also re-presses As Tradition Dies Slowly on vinyl that July.

years.h: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, July 23, 2015
yt: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, July 23, 2015

years.h: Survival Instinct, Morning Again's first new EP in 20 years
years.p: Written by email and text across state lines, it comes out on Revelation twenty years after As Tradition Dies Slowly.

eras.title: Borrowed time
eras.text: Morning Again settled into select shows and short tours rather than long runs, and the old singer came back when the current one couldn't.

years.h: Borrowed Time EP on Revelation
years.p: A second Revelation EP, followed by a European tour including Ieperfest in Ypres, Belgium, on July 2.

years.h: Damien Moyal fills in for injured Kevin Byers in Europe
years.p: With Kevin Byers out with a shoulder injury, Morning Again's first singer, Damien Moyal, takes the European tour.

sources.title: No Echo: Morning Again to return with new EP on Revelation
